newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela puts freeze on new cell phone customers.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela puts freeze on new cell phone customers.

text.p: Venezuela has barred the country's two cellular telephone companies from signing up new subscribers after a barrage of complaints about poor service and overbilling, a government minister said Tuesday.
"They are selling a terrible service, it's terribly congested," Transport and Communications Minister Moises Orozco told reporters, referring to the two companies, TELCEL and Movilent.
Until they expand their systems "we will not permit them to take on new subscribers," he said.

TelCel, which controls around 60 percent of the market, is 54 percent owned by BellSouth Corp of the United States. Movilnet is a wholly owned subsidiary of Venezuela's national telephone company CANTV.
"Greater competition is the only way to ensure better service," Orozco said, adding that two more cellphone concessions could be sold before the end of the year.
According to the telecommunications regulator Conatel, the two companies have added 200,000 subscribers in just the past few months.
With over 700,000 current users, or 35 mobile phones per 1,000 inhabitants, Venezuela has the highest rate of cell phone use in Latin America, Conatel said.
